mechanism: Replace rolling mean/StdDev bands with median ± k*(1.4826*MAD) over the same window; MAD has 50% breakdown so a single spike barely moves width while StdDev can inflate ~145%.
data_needed: OHLC closes (or chosen applied price) in a fixed rolling window; optional classical twins for comparison.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M30 breakdown demo (40-bar window); general FX/equity charts for indicators.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS a contamination-resistant volatility width that stays calibrated to sigma on clean data but does not balloon on gaps, bad ticks, or stop runs.
quote: That same single spike inflates the standard deviation from 0.000532 to 0.001304, a jump of about 145%, while the robust MAD-sigma moves from 0.000556 to 0.000563, barely more than 1%.

mechanism: Score latest close as (close - median)/(1.4826*MAD); spike registers on its own bar without shifting the zero line or compressing neighbors the way classical z-score does.
data_needed: Rolling window of closes; guard zero MAD on flat windows.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic MT5 charts; evidence on EURUSD M30.
why_new_for_mis: Provides a regime/extremeness sensor whose baseline is not hijacked by the outlier it is meant to detect.
quote: In a z-score oscillator, one spike inflates both the mean and the standard deviation, which shifts the zero line and compresses the reading of every other bar in the window. The MAD-score keeps its baseline steady.

mechanism: Fit trend as median of all pairwise slopes; size channel by 1.4826*MAD of residuals about that line so neither center nor width pivots on one spike (unlike OLS + residual StdDev).
data_needed: Rolling closes on modest window (O(n^2) pairwise slopes); ring buffer updates.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M30 contamination sweep; drop-in RobustTrend indicator.
why_new_for_mis: Robust trend-regime centerline that resists sign-flips from single bad ticks that reverse OLS slope.
quote: At row 1, one corrupted bar out of forty flips the least-squares slope from +0.000026 to -0.000002, a sign change. The Theil-Sen slope on the same row is still +0.000030, unchanged.

idea_name: Price-normalized quantile-channel Spread as vol feature
mechanism: Fit independent pinball/IRLS quantile lines (e.g. 0.1/0.5/0.9); Spread=Upper-Lower is a conditional IQR; divide by price so absolute width is not swamped by price-level trend; correlates with realised vol.
data_needed: Rolling window of applied prices; realised log-return StdDev for validation; relative IRLS convergence.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: BTCUSD, EURUSD, XAUUSD, SPX500 on D1 (also multi-TF width tables); window 100, tailProb 0.1.
why_new_for_mis: Distribution-free, asymmetric-capable volatility width that tracks realised vol after price normalisation, without assuming Gaussian residuals.
quote: Normalised by price, the correlation with contemporaneous realised volatility rises to 0.595. The third row looks one step ahead, against the next window's realised volatility: at 0.301 there is some leading information.

mechanism: Skew=(UpperGap-LowerGap)/Spread in [-1,1] because upper/lower quantiles are fitted independently; positive when upside half-width dominates.
data_needed: Three quantile lines on same window; Crossed() guard when lines invert.
why_new_for_mis: Reads upside vs downside dispersion asymmetry that symmetric Bollinger/regression bands cannot show.
quote: Because the two edges are fitted independently, the skew is free to be non-zero: it is positive when the upper half of the channel is the wider one and negative when the downside carries the wider tail.

mechanism: Treat normalised Spread as a regime variable: gate the same breakout rule on wide vs narrow channels (e.g. threshold 0.20) rather than using edges as entries.
data_needed: Normalised Spread series plus a base signal; Strategy Tester naive EA.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: BTCUSD D1 breakout with width gate; also EURUSD/XAUUSD/SPX500 D1 edge tests 2015–2026.
why_new_for_mis: Frames channel width as a regime filter for when a signal population differs, not as a predictive price bound.
quote: What can be said without overreaching is that the width behaves like a regime variable rather than a signal. The two gates split the same rule into two clearly different populations.

series_key: generative adversarial networks (gans) for synthetic data in financial modeling
idea_name: GAN rare-event and high-vol scenario synthesis
mechanism: Train Generator/Discriminator on historical prices (e.g. EURUSD) so synthetic paths include crashes, spikes, and consolidations scarce in archives; use for stress tests and robustness, validated with MSE/FID/KL/discriminator accuracy.
data_needed: Historical FX/OHLC series; GAN training loop; distribution metrics (MSE, FID, KL, discriminator ~50%).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD multi-year daily/synthetic comparison; MT5 synthetic candlestick demo.
why_new_for_mis: Supplies scarce high-vol/crash regime paths as sensing/stress inputs when historical samples under-represent those states.
quote: One of the areas of application we can identify is the field of risk assessment where GANs can model extreme market conditions and help to stress test portfolios without using historical data.

series_key: generative adversarial networks (gans) for synthetic data in financial modeling
idea_name: Levene variance fidelity of synthetic vs real
mechanism: After importing GAN CSV as MT5 custom symbol (SYNTH_EURUSD), compare real vs synthetic close variances with Levene's test (plus Shapiro–Wilk and t-test) to verify synthetic volatility structure matches live market.
data_needed: Aligned real and synthetic EURUSD closes; scipy levene/shapiro/ttest.
why_new_for_mis: Turns synthetic-data acceptance into an explicit volatility-structure sensor (equal variance) before using fake history in MIS stress pipelines.
quote: The validation proves that the synthetic data shows similar price volatility patterns which means it can accurately represent market behavior.

series_key: integrating ml models with the strategy tester
mechanism: MQL5 CFileCSV class (Open/WriteHeader/WriteLine/Read) for CSV messaging between Tester and Python; no market regime/vol/liquidity sensor.
why_new_for_mis: Infrastructure only after full read; no sensing idea.
quote: The CFileCSV class was designed to facilitate this interaction by allowing efficient data storage and loading.

mechanism: After MP denoising, subtract the leading eigenvector(s) with near-uniform loadings (shared market/regime tone) from the feature correlation matrix and re-correlate so family clusters separate.
data_needed: Feature panel (T×N) from one instrument; PCA of correlation; market_components count.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1-style engineered panel (trend, vol, microstructure, entropy, calendar); synthetic AR(1) mirror with T=1500.
why_new_for_mis: Extracts the shared regime/market factor that otherwise collapses distinct feature families into one cluster—usable as a common-tone sensor and as a cleaning step.
quote: Features derived from the same instrument's price path tend to share exposure to the prevailing regime: a trending, high-volatility stretch inflates trend, volatility, and several microstructure estimators simultaneously.

idea_name: AR(1) effective sample size for MP noise ceiling
mechanism: Replace raw bar count T in Marcenko–Pastur q=T/N by Teff=T*(1-ρ̄)/(1+ρ̄) from average lag-1 autocorrelation across feature columns; raises λmax and can drop marginal 'signal' eigenvalues.
data_needed: Feature matrix with serial correlation (H1 FX); eigenvalue histogram; absolute-bandwidth KDE.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: H1 FX bars; representative 30-feature panel ρ̄≈0.50 → Teff≈505 vs T=1500.
why_new_for_mis: Corrects overstated independence of FX bars so noise-vs-structure sensing (MP ceiling) matches effective information, not raw bar count.
quote: H1 FX bars are not independent; adjacent bars share regime, volatility clustering, and microstructural persistence, so T = raw bar count overstates the amount of independent information the panel actually contains.

mechanism: Constant-residual-eigenvalue denoise + detone, then ONC/K-means on √((1-ρ)/2); re-run on rolling/walk-forward windows because feature correlation drifts across regimes.
data_needed: Cleaned corr matrix; silhouette t-stat sweep over k; periodic refit cadence.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same EURUSD-like panel; ARI 0.23→0.83 after cleaning on synthetic truth.
why_new_for_mis: Turns regime-dependent feature codependence into a monitored clustering state that must be refreshed when market character changes.
quote: correlation structure among engineered features is not stationary across regimes. A denoising and clustering pass fit once on a multi-year window and never revisited will drift out of date.

series_key: online machine learning for trade signal filtering in mql5
idea_name: Online SGD logistic filter under regime shift
mechanism: Per-closed-trade SGD update of logistic weights on six scaled features; after a generative regime flip (feature weights change sign), online and rolling-batch recover separation while frozen stays negative.
data_needed: Binary win/loss labels including swap/commission; feature vector at entry; optional LR decay.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic 6-feature generator; planned real protocol EURUSD H1 (and GBPUSD, XAUUSD, index); EMA(12)/EMA(26) base signal.
why_new_for_mis: Native MQL5 sequence/online sensor that adapts filter probabilities when market relationships flip, without offline ONNX retrain.
quote: An online model facing the same shift sees its prediction error grow the moment the relationship flips, and the update pushes that weight down, then negative, over the trades that follow.

series_key: online machine learning for trade signal filtering in mql5
mechanism: x2 = ATRfast/ATRslow inside the online filter feature vector; scales short-horizon range against longer ATR as a local vol-regime input to P(win).
data_needed: Two ATR buffers plus other scaled features; closed-bar shift-1 reads.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any symbol EA runs on; evidence scripts synthetic; validation targets EURUSD H1.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit relative-volatility state in an adaptive probability sensor, not a static ADX threshold.
quote: x0 = RSI(14)/100  x1 = (close - EMAslow)/ATRfast  x2 = ATRfast/ATRslow

series_key: online machine learning for trade signal filtering in mql5
idea_name: Volume/SMA participation feature in online filter
mechanism: x5 = volume / SMA(volume,20) feeds participation intensity into online P(win); ablation shows it is weak alone on synthetic data but is the article's liquidity/context channel.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EA on liquid FX pairs; synthetic ablation tables.
why_new_for_mis: Online-updated participation/liquidity proxy coupled to trade-outcome feedback rather than a frozen volume filter.

mechanism: Uniform and CatBoost border methods (Median, Uniform, GreedyLogSum, etc.) compress predictor scales for tree models; preprocessing/encoding, not a market regime/vol/liquidity sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Random synthetic sample in Q_Trans script; CatBoost console examples.
why_new_for_mis: Full read is ML quantization theory and CatBoost plumbing; no market sensing construct.
quote: Data quantization is a method of compressing (encoding) observation information with an acceptable loss of accuracy in its measurement scale.

mechanism: Split sample into 1/10 chronological parts; exclude predictors whose part-wise means wander beyond a % of full-range mean (e.g. iVIDyA absolute price level)—a non-stationarity/regime-drift diagnostic on features.
data_needed: Train CSV predictors; chronological partitions; mean-spread threshold.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1 sample 2010-01-01 to 2023-09-01 via CB_Exp; iVIDyA_B0_S1_M1 example.
why_new_for_mis: Operational sensor for when a feature's level has shifted with the market so it must not enter MIS models as if stationary.
quote: This test allows excluding predictors whose indicators are highly shifted over time. Such predictors, in theory, impede training. An example of such a predictor can be seen in Figure 4... Variable Index Dynamic Average (iVIDyA).

mechanism: Group identical values into ranks; mark tails beyond ~2.5% each side as spikes (vs three-sigma); convert to boundary or random in-range values or drop rows—robust outlier fence for feature hygiene.
data_needed: Per-predictor value ranks; optional Proc_Vibros column.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD M1 CatBoost pipeline predictors (e.g. Vol_OHLC, iCCI).
why_new_for_mis: Distribution-aware spike sensor on engineered features that does not assume Gaussian three-sigma tails.
quote: To determine the spikes, I used 2.5% of the data for each side of the number series. The previously encountered identical number values were grouped and ranks were assigned to the groups.
